sections.admission_summary: Chief complaint: Sudden severe headache, vomiting, altered consciousness. Admitted for inpatient care.
sections.discharge_instructions: Drink plenty of fluids. Get adequate rest and avoid overexertion. Neurology/neurosurgery follow-up within 2-4 weeks. Repeat imaging per plan. Strict blood pressure control is essential. Do NOT restart anticoagulants without specialist approval. Strict blood pressure control (BP <140/90 target). Continue rehabilitation. Call ambulance immediately for severe headache, vomiting, weakness recurrence, or consciousness change. Activity restrictions per neurologist. Early rehabilitation as tolerated. Low-sodium diet. Blood pressure home monitoring twice daily.
sections.discharge_medications: Amlodipine 5mg PO daily x90d; Levetiracetam 500mg PO BID x30d
sections.follow_up: Neurology/neurosurgery follow-up within 2-4 weeks. Repeat imaging per plan.
sections.hospital_course: Length of stay: 12 days (primary reason: Sudden severe headache, vomiting, altered consciousness). Main treatment: other parenteral drugs (Nicardipine, Labetalol, Sodium Chloride 23.4% Injectable Solution). Key procedures: Urinary catheter insertion (2024-06-15), Nasogastric tube insertion (2024-06-15), Transthoracic echocardiography (2024-06-15), Central venous catheter insertion (2024-06-15), Craniotomy for intracranial hematoma evacuation (2024-06-15). Medication changes from admission: started Amlodipine, Levetiracetam. Condition at discharge: discharged home, Barthel Index 95/100.

sections.adl_assessment: Barthel Index 60/100 → moderate assistance (Feeding 5, Bathing 5, Mobility 10, Toilet use 5)
sections.care_plan: Care plan: Nursing problem: risk for raised intracranial pressure and altered neurological status. Goal: BP stays within the ordered range and neurological status does not worsen. Observation: Observe consciousness, pupils, weakness, headache and vomiting frequently and check BP; Assess swallowing. Care: Keep ordered BP control and bed rest with the head raised; Take fall precautions, reposition to prevent contracture and coordinate early rehabilitation. Education: Ask the patient to report headache, nausea or weakness at once.
